title: Almost Equal
summary: Determine whether the given pairwise-distinct strings can be reordered into a sequence where each adjacent pair differs in exactly one character.
requirements: Read N and M strings from stdin.
Decide whether a valid permutation exists.
Print Yes or No.
nonfunctional: Implement solve as a Rama deframafn; use Rama dataflow code for computation.
constraints: Strings contain lowercase English letters, have length M, and are pairwise distinct.
invariants: Every string appears exactly once in any candidate ordering.
Each consecutive pair must differ at exactly one character.
acceptance: Return Yes iff a permutation satisfies all consecutive-pair conditions; otherwise return No.
actors: Caller supplying one stdin-formatted input string.
environment: Standalone challenge function; no deployed Rama module is specified.
interfaces: Input: N, M, then N strings.
decisions: Treat strings as vertices and a one-character difference as a valid adjacency; determine if these vertices admit a path using every string.
tradeoffs: The small upper bound on N permits considering permutations; no production throughput or persistence requirements are specified.
seam: The challenge contract is a single solve(input-string) function, not a depot or query API.

flow.partition: Not applicable: standalone stdin/stdout algorithm; no Rama partitioning is specified.

caveat: Use Rama dataflow code. Local Clojure functions are prohibited.
